title: Pay insurance duty on premiums (insurers)
what: An insurer pays duty on the premiums for the insurance it writes in the state, and usually passes it on to the insured.

sources.title: Stamp Duties Act 1923 (SA)
sources.quote: (1) A general insurer who is, or is required to be, registered is liable under this section to pay duty in respect of each premium relating to insurance of any kind (other than life insurance) paid to the insurer

sources.title: Stamp Duties Act 1923 (SA)
sources.quote: (1) A general insurer who is, or is required to be, registered is liable under this section to pay duty in respect of each premium relating to insurance of any kind (other than life insurance) paid to the insurer

confidence_note: The Act's own words make the insurer liable for the duty (in the NT, the quote is the duty to register as an insurer before writing dutiable policies). Quoted from the Open Australian Legal Corpus copy of the official text, which is not itself official.

assessment.summary: A tax on insurance premiums on top of GST. It discourages people and businesses from insuring and leaves more risk unpooled; the Henry Review recommended abolishing all such taxes.

marks.reason: Raises the price of insurance relative to other services, so people under-insure (Henry Review).

assessment.confidence_note: The direction is well supported; no official estimate of the efficiency cost of insurance duty was found. Marks copied from the register item sa-insurance-duty so the two agree.
